what: Fail open when the rate limiter's backing store is unavailable
why: a cache outage must not take down the write path

what: Fail closed on auth service errors
why: deny the request rather than admit unauthenticated traffic

what: Retry failed calls with exponential backoff plus random jitter
why: jitter prevents a thundering herd on recovery

what: Do not retry non-idempotent writes
why: a duplicate charge is worse than a failed one

what: Implement rate limiting server-side as middleware or in the gateway
why: client-side limits are advisory and trivially bypassed

what: Disable rate limiting for internal service-to-service calls
why: internal callers are already capacity-planned and limiting them causes cascading retries

what: Wrap synchronous downstream calls in a circuit breaker
why: failing fast frees caller resources and lets the downstream recover

what: Drain in-flight connections on graceful shutdown before exit
why: killing live requests surfaces as user-visible 502s during every deploy

what: ClickHouse is the sole store for orders with no MySQL dual-write
why: breakdown, snapshot and trend reads all resolve from one source, avoiding divergence

what: MySQL order_events is the source of truth and the ClickHouse tables are best-effort replicas
why: writes go to both stores, so one authoritative store avoids divergence

what: Money must be stored as int64 cents and never as a float
why: float rounding caused a reconciliation incident

what: Configure the service via environment variables in a configs directory
why: keeps deployment config out of the binary and out of version control

what: Write middleware with the standard net/http handler signature
why: keeps middleware composable with anything in the ecosystem

what: Emit structured JSON logs with a correlation id on every request
why: unstructured logs cannot be joined across services during an incident

what: Add application-level trace spans inside handlers
why: framework spans stop at the handler boundary and hide the slow part

what: Run database migrations forward-only with an explicit rollback script
why: auto-rollback on a partially applied migration corrupts more than it fixes

what: Set logging verbosity with the LOG_LEVEL environment variable
why: changing verbosity must not require a redeploy during an incident

what: Propagate context deadlines across every internal service call
why: a call without a deadline can outlive the request that started it

what: Cache read-heavy endpoints behind a short TTL with stale-while-revalidate
why: a stampede on expiry is worse than serving a slightly stale response

what: Never log request bodies containing payment details
why: logs are replicated widely and retained far longer than the data policy allows
